overview: Two similarly-named but very different tubes of the urinary system, easily confused because of how close their names sound.
genZNote: Ureter: carries urine from kidney to bladder. Urethra: carries it from bladder to the outside.

aspects.label: What It Connects
aspects.valueA: Connects each kidney to the urinary bladder.
aspects.valueB: Connects the urinary bladder to the outside of the body.

aspects.label: Length Difference by Sex
aspects.valueA: Roughly the same length in both sexes.
aspects.valueB: Significantly shorter in females than in males, which is why females have a higher risk of urinary tract infections.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The urethra's shorter length in females is a frequently tested reason for their higher susceptibility to urinary tract infections (UTIs).
overlay.memoryTrick: Ureter (with an 'e') carries urine from kidnEy. Urethra sounds like 'exit-thra' — carries urine out.
overlay.commonMisconception: These two names are not interchangeable despite sounding similar — mixing them up is one of the most common spelling/concept errors in anatomy exams.
